chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Asama, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Rain falls on me while I am wearing a garment, so it becomes wet, and I am in a state of major ritual impurity (junub). If some of the semen that touched my body also touches the garment, can I pray in it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.أُصَلِّي فِيهِ: Pray in it (referring to the garment)
key_terms.السَّمَاء: The sky, here referring to rain falling from it
key_terms.جُنُب: State of major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)

ai.seo_question: Can I pray in my clothes if rain wets them while I am in a state of major impurity (junub)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that rainwater does not invalidate the ritual purity of a garment worn by a *junub* (person in major impurity), even if residual semen transfers to it, establishing that the garment remains valid for prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the state of major impurity (*hadath akbar*) and the physical substance of semen (*mani*), affirming that the garment's validity is not compromised by the presence of the impurity itself when wetted by rain. It underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) in ritual purification, where the focus remains on the removal of the impurity rather than the state of the wearer.
